name: Gold
title: Where all the gold is: who owns it, where it's stored, and how much is left
description: About 216,000 tonnes of gold have been mined. See who owns it (central banks, the IMF, ETFs), where it sits, what's left in the ground, and a live mining clock. USGS and IMF data.

blocks.headline: Only about 16.6% of all gold ever mined has a publicly named owner.

blocks.title: Approx. gold ever mined (USGS cumulative production)
lines: USGS: about 187,000 t "historically produced" (the FAQ pairs this with 57,000 t of reserves, the MCS 2017 figure, so it's read here as through end-2016). [[usgsfaq]]
Cross-check: USGS year-by-year world production 1900–2025 alone sums to 185,173 t; the rest (~30,817 t) was mined before 1900.

blocks.title: Who owns it (the math)
lines: Central banks & governments: 31,221.9 t, the sum of the latest monthly gold holdings of 79 reporters to the IMF (including the ECB). [[irfcl]]
ETFs: GLD 1,041.65 + IAU 463.05 + GLDM 234.85 = 1,739.55 t, from each issuer's own published holdings. [[gld]] [[iau]] [[gldm]]
Tether: 146.19 t backing USDT + 22.01 t backing XAU₮ = 168.2 t (Jun 30, 2026). [[tether]]
Disclosed individuals: none. No person's personal bullion holding is publicly verified.
Privately held, owner not public = 215,990 − 35,943.8 = **180,046.2 t (83.4%)**
blocks.note: The "owner not public" bucket is everything without a named holder: jewelry, private bars and coins, gold in other ETFs and funds, industrial gold, gold lost over history, and any official gold not reported to the IMF. Dates differ by row. Treat all shares as approximate.

blocks.text: Jewelry is the largest single use of newly consumed gold, according to USGS's 2026 summary. [[mcs26]]

sections.lede: Official gold reported to the IMF by 79 central banks and governments: 31,221.9 t in total. Top 20, latest month reported.

blocks.note: Source: International Monetary Fund, International Reserves and Foreign Currency Liquidity (IRFCL), gold volume in fine troy ounces ÷ 32,150.75. Brazil's value is reported in thousandths of an ounce and was divided by 1,000; Angola and Kosovo were left out because their units look wrong. Some holders (for example several Gulf states, Uzbekistan, Iraq and Taiwan) don't report gold in IRFCL and aren't counted. [[irfcl]]

sections.title: Still in the ground
sections.lede: World reserves: about 66,000 t (USGS). At 2025's pace that's about 20 years of mining (66,000 ÷ 3,300, derived). Reserves get revised up as prices rise and new deposits are proven, so this isn't a countdown. [[mcs26]]

sections.title: Timeline
sections.lede: Big events, breakthroughs, people and places.

items.text: Earliest known worked gold, in the Varna necropolis.
First coins, struck in electrum, a natural gold-silver alloy. Pure gold coins follow under Croesus, c. 560–540 BC.
California Gold Rush.
Australian gold rush.
Gold discovered on the Witwatersrand, the basin that has produced more gold than anywhere else.
Klondike Gold Rush.
The London Gold Fixing begins.
Executive Order 6102 bans most private gold ownership in the US.
Gold Reserve Act becomes law. The next day, Roosevelt resets the price from $20.67 to $35 an ounce.
First gold arrives at Fort Knox.
Fort Knox holdings peak at 649.6M oz.
Bretton Woods pegs the dollar to gold at $35 and creates the IMF.
Muruntau discovered; now one of the largest gold mines.
The London Gold Pool defends the $35 price.
Newmont starts open-pit mining on the newly found Carlin Trend.
Nixon closes the gold window, ending dollar convertibility.
US official gold price set at $42.22/oz, still the book value today.
The New York Fed vault peaks at more than 12,000 t.
Private gold ownership becomes legal again in the US.
Price spikes to $850/oz.
Grasberg discovered.
Washington Agreement caps European central-bank gold sales at about 400 t a year. The UK sells 395 t from 1999 to 2002 at an average of about $275/oz.
GLD launches, making gold trade like a stock.
iShares Gold Trust (IAU) launches.
Then-record of about $1,900/oz.
The LBMA Gold Price replaces the London Fix.
Polyus wins the rights to Sukhoi Log (40 Moz of reserves).
Barrick and Newmont form the Nevada Gold Mines joint venture (61.5% / 38.5%).
All-time high of $5,501.70/oz (LBMA AM).
Price falls about 27% from the peak, to about $4,026 (Jun 30 PM).
London vaults hold a record 9,821 t; the Bank of England holds 5,782 t.
